notes: id_scheme: every rule has a permanent `id`. IDs never change or get reused between versions; a retired rule keeps its id with `retired: true`. Prefixes: tr.* = training_rules, pr.* = progression_rules, sf.* = screening (questions cited as sf.screening.<question id>); safety red-flag rules keep their bare snake_case ids from v0.1.0. AI suggestions must cite ids, e.g. 'pr.stall.step2'.
Actions (most to least urgent): stop_now_call_999 | stop_and_contact_111 | stop_and_see_gp | reduce_or_rest | modify_exercise | continue_with_caution.
These rules run in code BEFORE and AFTER the LLM. The LLM can never downgrade an action.
Messages are ours (UK English, calm). Not medical advice; the app should say so once in onboarding.

rules.red_flag: Sudden chest pain/discomfort that doesn't go away; OR pain spreading to arm, neck, jaw, stomach or back; OR chest pain with sweating, feeling sick, light-headedness or breathlessness.
rules.user_message: Please stop now and call 999. Chest pain like this needs checking straight away. Stay still and don't drive yourself.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Known angina: symptoms still there 5 minutes after the second GTN dose.
rules.user_message: If your angina hasn't eased 5 minutes after your second spray, call 999 now.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Chest pain, palpitations, dizziness or light-headedness DURING exercise.
rules.user_message: Let's stop here and rest. If it doesn't settle quickly, call 999. If it settles, please see your GP before training again.

rules.escalate_if: not settling quickly, or any chest_pain_emergency feature present
rules.gap: No source gives a minute threshold; escalate on any doubt.

rules.red_flag: Chest pain that comes and goes, or passed quickly but the user is still worried.
rules.user_message: Chest pain that comes and goes is worth a GP visit. Let's keep things light until you've been seen.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Angina getting worse, more frequent, lasting longer, or happening at rest.
rules.user_message: This change needs checking today. Please contact NHS 111.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: User unsure whether a symptom is serious.
rules.user_message: If you're not sure how serious it is, NHS 111 can check your symptoms and tell you what to do.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Injury with a crack sound, deformity/odd angle, numbness or pins and needles, or skin blue/grey/cold.
rules.user_message: Please stop and go to A&E, or call 999. This may need an X-ray or urgent care.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Can't bear weight or walk more than a few steps; pain or swelling severe or worsening; signs of infection (high temperature, hot/shivery).
rules.user_message: Let's rest that area. Please contact NHS 111 today.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Suspected sprain or strain (pain, swelling, bruising after a twist or overstretch).
rules.user_message: Protect it, rest, ice, compress and elevate for 2-3 days. We'll ease back in gradually and work around it.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.
rules.engine_action: Exclude exercises loading the flagged body area; resume at 50% volume.

rules.red_flag: Calf that is hot, swollen, tender and tense to touch.
rules.user_message: Please stop and get medical help now. A hot, swollen, tender calf needs checking today.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Localised ache or injury not settling within 6 weeks.
rules.user_message: This has gone on longer than usual. A GP or physio should take a look.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Dull, general muscle soreness starting 1-3 days after a hard or new session, easing within ~5 days.
rules.user_message: That sounds like normal soreness after a harder session. Light movement helps and it should ease in a few days.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.
rules.engine_action: Allow training; avoid hard sets on the sore muscle until soreness is mild.

rules.red_flag: Soreness lasting more than 7 days; sharp or constant pain; severe swelling around a muscle; pain in a joint rather than muscle.
rules.user_message: This doesn't sound like normal soreness. Please rest that area and see your GP.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.

rules.red_flag: Dark or blood-tinged (cola-coloured) urine after exercise, especially with severe muscle pain or weakness.
rules.user_message: Dark urine after a hard session needs checking today. Please contact NHS 111 and drink water.
rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.
rules.escalate_if: severe pain, weakness or very little urine
rules.gap: Escalation is our inference; no NHS page found.

rules.red_flag: Illness with symptoms above the neck only (runny nose, congestion, mild sore throat).
rules.user_message: Light movement is usually fine with a head cold. Let's halve today's effort.

sources.title: Should you exercise when you're sick?

rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.
rules.engine_action: Cut volume and intensity by >=50%; low-impact only.
rules.gap: 'Neck check' is a US rule of thumb, not NHS guidance; label as guidance.

rules.red_flag: Fever, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, vomiting, diarrhoea, body aches or whole-body fatigue.
rules.user_message: Your body needs rest to recover. A few days off won't undo your progress.

sources.title: Should you exercise when you're sick?

rules.licence: Facts/figures cited from source; wording is ours. No source text reproduced.
rules.engine_action: No training until symptom-free; then 1 week at maintenance dose.

rules.red_flag: Missed 3 periods in a row, or cycle has become irregular, alongside heavy training or weight loss.
rules.user_message: Missed periods can be a sign your body isn't getting enough energy for your training. Please see your GP. We'll ease the load in the meantime.

rules.red_flag: Ongoing fatigue and poor recovery, bone stress injury, falling libido, low mood, rapid weight loss, or feeling compelled to exercise. Any sex, any level.
rules.user_message: Some of what you've described can happen when training outpaces fuel. It's worth a GP check. Let's lighten the plan and look at recovery.

questions.text: In the last 3 months, have you done at least 30 minutes of planned moderate exercise on 3 or more days a week?
Has a doctor ever told you that you have a heart, metabolic (e.g. diabetes) or kidney condition?

Do you ever get any of these: chest, jaw or arm discomfort; breathlessness at rest or with light effort; dizziness or fainting; breathlessness lying flat; ankle swelling; a racing or fluttering heartbeat; calf pain when walking; a known heart murmur; or unusual tiredness with everyday activity?
Do you have a bone, joint or muscle problem that exercise could make worse?
Has a doctor told you to only exercise under medical supervision?

screening.questions_note: Our own wording based on ACSM screening criteria. NOT PAR-Q+ (see parq_licence).

symptoms=yes.message: Please check with your GP before starting. We'll be here when you're ready.

supervised_only=yes.message: Your doctor has asked for supervised exercise, so please start with them first.

msk_issue=yes.engine_action: Flag area; exclude/modify exercises loading it; suggest physio.

screening.recheck: Ask the symptoms question again if the user logs any pain/dizziness flag, and every 6 months.
